```{r}
#| label: helper-functions
#| include: false
# Set shared plot sizes and typography so figures stay visually consistent.
gg_fig_width <- 11
gg_base_size <- 12
gg_title_size <- 17
gg_subtitle_size <- 13.5
gg_caption_size <- 10.5
gg_strip_size <- 12
gg_axis_size <- 10
gg_annot_size <- 3.7
gg_plot_family <- "Noto Sans"

# Define a reusable ggplot theme for all RIS figures in the post.
ris_plot_theme <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = gg_base_size, base_family = gg_plot_family) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.title = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        hjust = 0,
        halign = 0,
        size = gg_title_size,
        family = gg_plot_family,
        face = "bold",
        color = "#1F2933",
        lineheight = 1.1,
        width = grid::unit(1, "npc"),
        margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 8)
      ),
      plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        color = "#52616B",
        size = gg_subtitle_size,
        family = gg_plot_family,
        lineheight = 1.15,
        width = grid::unit(1, "npc"),
        margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 4, b = 12)
      ),
      plot.caption = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        color = "#52616B",
        hjust = 0,

# Register Noto Sans for SVG output so exported graphics keep the same typeface.
noto_sans_svg_fonts <- list(
  systemfonts::fonts_as_import(
    gg_plot_family,
    weight = c("normal", "bold"),
    type = "import",
    repositories = NULL,
    may_embed = TRUE
  )
)

# Open SVG devices with the configured web fonts for Quarto figures.
svg_noto <- function(filename, width, height, ...) {
  svglite::svglite(
    filename = filename,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    web_fonts = noto_sans_svg_fonts,
    ...
  )
}

# Store the common source and credit text appended to figure captions.
ris_graph_caption_end <- paste0(
  "<br><br>Data: Austrian Legal Information System (RIS) via {risAT} package",
  "<br>Graphic: Roland Schmidt, https&#58;//werk.statt.codes | Bluesky: @zoowalk.bsky.social"
)

# Append the shared RIS source and credit text to a figure-specific caption.
ris_graph_caption <- function(text) {
  paste0(text, ris_graph_caption_end)
}

# Format RIS result tibbles consistently, including readable list-column cells.
style_ris_table <- function(data) {
  column_defs <- list(
    decision_date = colDef(name = "Date", minWidth = 95),
    case_number = colDef(name = "Case number", minWidth = 130),
    application = colDef(name = "RIS application", minWidth = 110),
    document_type = colDef(name = "Document type", minWidth = 120),
    query_topic = colDef(name = "Topic", minWidth = 130),
    norms = colDef(
      name = "Norms",
      cell = function(value) {
        paste(normalise_norm_values(value), collapse = "; ")
      }
    ),
    url = colDef(
      name = "RIS link",
      html = TRUE,
      cell = function(value) {
        if (is.na(value) || !nzchar(value)) {
          return("")
        }
        sprintf("<a href='%s' target='_blank'>open</a>", value)
      }
    )
  )
  column_defs <- column_defs[names(column_defs) %in% names(data)]

  reactable(
    data,
    searchable = TRUE,
    filterable = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 8,
    highlight = TRUE,
    bordered = TRUE,
    striped = TRUE,
    compact = TRUE,
    columns = column_defs
  )
}

# Pick one usable content URL per result, preferring the requested format.
first_content_url <- function(data, format = "Html") {
  if (!"content_urls" %in% names(data)) {
    data$content_urls <- vector("list", nrow(data))
  }

  data |>
    mutate(
      url = map_chr(content_urls, \(x) {
        if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) {
          return(NA_character_)
        }

        urls <- as.character(x)
        urls <- urls[!is.na(urls)]

        if (length(urls) == 0) {
          return(NA_character_)
        }

        preferred <- urls[str_detect(str_to_lower(urls), str_to_lower(format))]
        if (length(preferred) > 0) {
          return(preferred[[1]])
        }

        urls[[1]]
      })
    )
}

# Build a compact table of recent decisions with direct RIS links.
prepare_ris_link_table <- function(data, n = 12) {
  data <- first_content_url(data)

  display_cols <- c("decision_date", "case_number", "document_type", "url")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(display_cols, names(data))

  for (col in missing_cols) {
    data[[col]] <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
  }

  data |>
    select(all_of(display_cols)) |>
    arrange(desc(decision_date)) |>
    slice_head(n = n)
}

# Expand all available content URLs into one row per linked format.
prepare_content_urls_table <- function(data, n = 12) {
  if (!"content_urls" %in% names(data)) {
    data$content_urls <- vector("list", nrow(data))
  }

  display_cols <- c("decision_date", "case_number", "content_urls")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(display_cols, names(data))

  for (col in missing_cols) {
    if (col == "content_urls") {
      data[[col]] <- vector("list", nrow(data))
    } else {
      data[[col]] <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(data))
    }
  }

  data |>
    select(all_of(display_cols)) |>
    unnest_longer(content_urls, values_to = "url", keep_empty = TRUE) |>
    mutate(
      format = case_when(
        str_detect(str_to_lower(url), "pdf") ~ "PDF",
        str_detect(str_to_lower(url), "html") ~ "HTML",
        TRUE ~ "RIS"
      )
    ) |>
    select(decision_date, case_number, format, url) |>
    arrange(desc(decision_date)) |>
    slice_head(n = n)
}

# Collapse scalar list-columns into displayable strings for combined results.
collapse_scalar_list_col <- function(x) {
  map_chr(x, \(value) {
    if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0 || all(is.na(value))) {
      return(NA_character_)
    }

    paste(unique(as.character(value)), collapse = "; ")
  })
}

# Normalize one norms value from either legacy comma-separated text or a list entry.
normalise_norm_values <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0 || all(is.na(x))) {
    return(character())
  }

  values <- as.character(unlist(x, use.names = FALSE))

  if (length(values) == 1) {
    values <- str_split(values, ",\\s*")[[1]]
  }

  values |>
    str_squish() |>
    discard(\(value) is.na(value) || value == "")
}

# Normalize the full norms column while keeping it as a list-column.
normalise_norms_column <- function(x) {
  map(x, normalise_norm_values)
}

# Test whether any normalized norm value matches a case-insensitive pattern.
has_matching_norm <- function(x, pattern) {
  any(str_detect(normalise_norm_values(x), regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Collapse scalar list-columns while preserving true list-columns used downstream.
normalise_ris_result_types <- function(data) {
  scalar_list_cols <- names(data)[map_lgl(data, is.list)]
  scalar_list_cols <- setdiff(scalar_list_cols, c("content_urls", "app_metadata", "norms"))

  if (length(scalar_list_cols) == 0) {
    return(data)
  }

  data |>
    mutate(across(all_of(scalar_list_cols), collapse_scalar_list_col))
}

# Combine named RIS result sets into one tibble, optionally recording the source name.
bind_ris_results <- function(results, names_to = NULL) {
  imap(
    results,
    \(data, name) {
      data <- normalise_ris_result_types(data)

      if (!is.null(names_to)) {
        data[[names_to]] <- name
      }

      data
    }
  ) |>
    list_rbind()
}
```

# Context & Purpose

The Austrian Legal Information System, [RIS](https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/), short for *Rechtsinformationssystem*, is the central public repository of Austrian law and jurisprudence. Broadly speaking, it provides access to Austria's current and historical legal norms, including federal and state law, as well as to the jurisprudence of the country's most important courts and judicial institutions. The latter covers the case law of the Constitutional Court (*Verfassungsgerichtshof*, VfGH), the Administrative Court (*Verwaltungsgerichtshof*, VwGH), the Federal Administrative Court (*Bundesverwaltungsgericht*, BVwG), and decisions by institutions such as the Equal Treatment Commission, the Data Protection Authority, and the Federal Disciplinary Board.

This wealth of information makes RIS an indispensable source for anyone working on issues related to the Austrian legal system. While accessing the data is straightforward via the official website, accessing RIS data in bulk and analyzing it beyond individual cases has mostly required tinkering with the service's API and wrangling the returned JSON results. The new R package {risAT} aims to lower this barrier by providing an intuitive and efficient way to work with RIS data and make it amenable to analysis beyond the single case. The package wraps the RIS Open Government Data REST API and returns tidy tibbles with standardized English column names, while preserving the links and metadata needed to inspect the original RIS records. With this, {risAT} can be helpful to researchers, students, and journalists who work in R and are interested in the Austrian legal framework. {risAT} can serve, e.g., as a starting point for text mining and text analysis when collecting the required corpus; similarly, the package can be used to produce descriptive statistics on the frequency of specific decisions by a particular court and how this frequency has developed over time. Whenever you are interested in more than one case, {risAT} can come handy.

Please note that the package is still under development (`0.0.1`) and that its interface may change. Furthermore, the package is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by RIS or the Austrian Federal Chancellery.

You can install {risAT} from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("werkstattcodes/{risAT}")
```

For the full function reference, see the [documentation site](https://werkstattcodes.github.io/risAT/) and the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/werkstattcodes/risAT/). If you want to receive updates on releases, I would recommend subscribing to the repo on Github. For any questions or suggestions, please use the discussion board or file an issue on the GitHub page.

And you if you use the package in a publication, please cite it as follows:

# Scope

The RIS API organises case law by *application*. In practice, that means one application for each court system or specialised decision-making body. {risAT} provides convenience wrappers for the main courts, plus a generic search function:

| Function | Court / Body |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `ris_search_vfgh()` | Constitutional Court (*Verfassungsgerichtshof*, VfGH) |
| `ris_search_vwgh()` | Administrative Court (*Verwaltungsgerichtshof*, VwGH) |
| `ris_search_justiz()` | Ordinary courts (*OGH, OLG, LG, BG*) |
| `ris_search_bvwg()` | Federal Administrative Court (*Bundesverwaltungsgericht*, BVwG) |
| `ris_search_lvwg()` | State administrative courts (*Landesverwaltungsgerichte*, LVwG) |
| `ris_search_dsk()` | Data protection authorities |
| `ris_search_dok()` | Disciplinary body decisions |
| `ris_search_pvak()` | Staff representation oversight |
| `ris_search_gbk()` | Equal Treatment Commission (*Gleichbehandlungskommission*) |
| `ris_search_case_law()` | Generic wrapper for any supported case-law application |

The court-specific functions are thin wrappers around `ris_search_case_law()`.

Every result includes standard columns such as `id`, `application`, `decision_date`, `case_number`, and `document_type`. It also includes list-columns such as `content_urls`, which stores links to the RIS HTML and PDF records. 

With `echo = TRUE`, {risAT} prints the equivalent RIS web search URL and the number of returned rows. This is useful because it lets you move between the reproducible R workflow and the browser interface that many legal researchers already know.

![](_img/chunkWithEcho.png){fig-align="left"}




# Examples

The examples below are meant to show the kinds of questions one can start asking once RIS case law is available as data. They are not full analyses, and the query choices are intentionally transparent so that they can be adjusted for more careful research designs. 

## VfGH - European Convention on Human Rights

To start with, let's use {risAT} to query the data on the decisions of the Austrian Constitutional Court, the Verfassungsgerichtshof (VfGH). Considering the special status of the European Convention for Human Rights (ECHR; it is directly applicable in Austria), I was wondering how frequently the VfGH refers to norms of the ECHR in its decisions. To answer this, the code below

1.  retrieves the meta data on all decisions of the VfGH from the beginning of 2000 to the end of 2025, and
2.  checks whether the ECHR is referenced among the norms invoked in each of the decisions. The `norms` column, returned by the API, stipulates the norms in question.

```{r}
#| include: false

vfgh_2000_2025 <- readr::read_rds(data_path("vfgh", "vfgh_2000_2025.rds"))
```

```{r}
vfgh_2000_2025 %>%
  count(document_type)

library(janitor)
janitor::get_dupes(vfgh_2000_2025, id)
janitor::get_dupes(vfgh_2000_2025, case_number)

```

Here is the relevant function call via {risAT}'s `ris_search_vfgh()`[^1]:

[^1]: This call is rather comprehensive and can be quite time consuming. To add a layer of robustness, you may want to split it into separate calls for each year, store the interim results, and then combine them. Also a note on the netiquette: The RIS API is a public service, and it is important to avoid overloading it with too many requests in a short time. Please be considerate and avoid sending too many requests in quick succession.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Get all decisions by the Constitutional Court (VfGH)"
#| eval: false
vfgh_2000_2025 <- ris_search_vfgh(
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
) 
```

In total we get data on `r nrow(vfgh_2000_2025)` decisions. Below is a glimpse of the data structure, which shows the main columns and their types. The `norms` column is a list-column, which means that each row can contain multiple norms.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Describe result"
glimpse(vfgh_2000_2025)
```

In the next step, let's check which of the decisions obtained above make reference to the ECHR and calculate the annual totals of decisions with and without such a reference. The code below extracts the year from the `decision_date` column, checks for ECHR references in the `norms` column, and calculates annual totals and shares.

To avoid duplicates, we only look at the decisions of type "text", and not "Rechtssatz" (which is summary of the legal essence of a decision).

```{r}
#| label: vfgh-data-year
#| cache: true
#| code-summary: "Identify VfGH decisions with ECHR norm reference"

class(vfgh_2000_2025$norms)
table(vfgh_2000_2025$document_type)

#keep only decisions of type "Text"
vfgh_2000_2025_echr <- vfgh_2000_2025 %>%
  filter(document_type=="Text") 

nrow(vfgh_2000_2025_echr)  


#extract year; check for ECHR reference in norms
#add dummy TRUE if norms (list) contains at least one reference to the EMRK
vfgh_2000_2025_echr <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  mutate(year=year(decision_date)) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_echr = map_lgl(norms, \(x) any(str_detect(as.character(unlist(x)), fixed("EMRK")), na.rm = TRUE))
  )

#calculate annual totals (and labels for later plotting)
vfgh_year <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  count(year, norm_echr) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_reference = factor(
      if_else(norm_echr, "Norm references ECHR", "General decisions"),
      levels = c("Norm references ECHR", "General decisions")
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    share = n / total,
    echr_label = if_else(norm_echr, scales::percent(share, accuracy = 1), NA_character_)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

Now let's visualize the results.

```{r}
#| label: vfgh-plot-year
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
#| cache: true
#| code-summary: "Identify VfGH decisions with ECHR norm reference"
#| code-fold: true

vfgh_year_totals <- vfgh_year %>%
  distinct(year, total) %>%
  filter(total > 0)


vfgh_year %>%
ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n, fill=norm_reference)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  geom_text(
    data = vfgh_year_totals,
    aes(x = year, y = total, label = total),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.35,
    color = "black",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = echr_label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "black",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2025, 5),
  expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("General decisions" = "#1F3A5F", "Norm references ECHR" = "#D4A017"),
    name = "Norm reference"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Constitutional Court decisions referencing the ECHR",
    subtitle = "Decisions by year, with decisions containing a norm reference to the European Convention on Human Rights highlighted.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VfGH decisions from 2000 to 2025 by decision year, highlighting decisions with a norm reference to the European Convention on Human Rights.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(
    legend.location = "plot",
    legend.justification.top = "left",
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )
```

As you can see -- ignoring the plotting code -- only a few lines of code yield a clear picture on the presence of the EMRK in decisions of the Austrian Constitutional Court. The graph above shows the annual number of decisions by the VfGH, highlighting those which contain a norm reference to the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). Both the number and the share of decisions referencing the ECHR have increased over time, with a notable surge in recent years.

We can further refine the analysis by looking at the actual paragraphs of the ECHR which are referenced in the decisions. The code below extracts the article and paragraph numbers from the `norms` column, counts the occurrences of each combination, and displays the results.


```{r}

vfgh_2000_2025_echr <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  filter(norm_echr==TRUE) %>% #keep only decisions with at least one norm reference to the ECHR
  mutate(norms=map(norms, normalise_norm_values)) %>% #standardize the norms column (elements of differnt class)
  unnest_longer(norms) #unnest

class(vfgh_2000_2025_echr$norms)

echr_decisions_total <- n_distinct(vfgh_2000_2025_echr$id)

echr_norm_names <- tibble::tribble(
  ~ZP_type, ~art, ~norm_short,
  NA_character_, "1", "Respect for human rights",
  NA_character_, "2", "Right to life",
  NA_character_, "3", "Prohibition of torture",
  NA_character_, "4", "Slavery and forced labour",
  NA_character_, "5", "Liberty and security",
  NA_character_, "6", "Fair trial",
  NA_character_, "7", "No punishment without law",
  NA_character_, "8", "Private and family life",
  NA_character_, "9", "Thought, conscience and religion",
  NA_character_, "10", "Expression",
  NA_character_, "11", "Assembly and association",
  NA_character_, "12", "Marriage",
  NA_character_, "13", "Effective remedy",
  NA_character_, "14", "Discrimination",
  NA_character_, "15", "Emergency derogation",
  NA_character_, "16", "Political activity of aliens",
  NA_character_, "17", "Abuse of rights",
  NA_character_, "18", "Use of restrictions",
  "1. ZP", "1", "Property",
  "1. ZP", "2", "Education",
  "1. ZP", "3", "Free elections",
  "4. ZP", "1", "No imprisonment for debt",
  "4. ZP", "2", "Freedom of movement",
  "4. ZP", "3", "No expulsion of nationals",
  "4. ZP", "4", "Collective expulsion",
  "6. ZP", "1", "Abolition of death penalty",
  "7. ZP", "1", "Expulsion safeguards",
  "7. ZP", "2", "Criminal appeal",
  "7. ZP", "3", "Wrongful conviction",
  "7. ZP", "4", "Double jeopardy",
  "7. ZP", "5", "Spousal equality",
  "12. ZP", "1", "General discrimination",
  "13. ZP", "1", "Death penalty abolition"
)

norm_count <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  filter(str_detect(norms, regex("EMRK"))) %>% #keep only EMRK norms
  mutate(
    ZP=str_detect(norms, regex("ZP")), #identify references to an additional protocol of th ECHR
    ZP_type=str_extract(norms, regex("\\d\\.?\\s+ZP"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_split=str_split(norms, regex(",s*")) #split norm if it contains multiple artiles
  ) %>%
  unnest_longer(norm_split) %>% 
  mutate(art=str_extract(norm_split, regex("(?<=Art)\\d+")))  %>% #extract article
  mutate(abs=str_extract(norm_split, regex("(?<=Abs)\\d+")))   %>% #extract paragraph
  distinct(id, ZP_type, art, abs) %>%
  count(ZP_type, art, abs, sort=T) %>%
  mutate(label=str_squish(str_c(
    coalesce(str_c(ZP_type, ", "), ""),
    coalesce(str_c("Art. ", art), ""),
    coalesce(str_c(", Abs. ", abs), "")
  ))) %>%
  left_join(echr_norm_names, by = join_by(ZP_type, art)) %>%
  mutate(norm_short = coalesce(norm_short, "ECHR norm"))
  

```


```{r}
#| label: vfgh-echr-top-norms
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
#| code-summary: "Plot the most frequent ECHR norm references"
#| code-fold: true


norm_count_top <- norm_count %>%
  mutate(label = forcats::fct_lump_n(label, n = 10, w = n, other_level = "all other ECHR norms referenced.")) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(n),
    norm_short = if_else(
      n_distinct(norm_short) == 1,
      first(norm_short),
      "Other ECHR norms"
    ),
    .by = label
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rel = n / echr_decisions_total,
    bar_label = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", n, rel * 100),
    label = forcats::fct_reorder(label, n),
    label = forcats::fct_relevel(label, "all other ECHR norms referenced.", after = 0)
  )

left_axis_labels <- norm_count_top %>%
  mutate(
    label_md = str_c(
      # escape leading "1." etc. so gridtext doesn't parse it as an ordered list
      str_replace_all(str_wrap(as.character(label), 15), "\n", "<br>") |>
        str_replace("^(\\d+)\\.", "\\1\\\\."),
      if_else(
        label == "all other ECHR norms referenced.",
        "", # short name would be redundant here
        str_c(
          "<br><span style='font-size:8pt;color:#52616B'>(",
          str_replace_all(str_wrap(norm_short, 22), "\n", "<br>"),
          ")</span>"
        )
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  { setNames(.$label_md, as.character(.$label)) }

vfgh_decisions_total <- sum(vfgh_year$n)
echr_share <- echr_decisions_total / vfgh_decisions_total

norm_count_top %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = label)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1F3A5F", width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = bar_label),
    hjust = -0.15,
    color = "#263238",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.18)))+
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) left_axis_labels[x]) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Which norms of the European Convention on Human Rights does the Austrian Constitutional Court reference most often?",
    subtitle = str_glue(
      "Between 2000 and 2025, the Austrian Constitutional Court (VfGH) issued ",
      "{scales::comma(vfgh_decisions_total)} decisions. ",
      "{scales::comma(echr_decisions_total)} of them ({scales::percent(echr_share, accuracy = 0.1)}) ",
      "contain a norm reference to the ECHR. The chart shows the most frequently referenced ",
      "Convention norms; percentages give the share of ECHR-referencing decisions citing each norm. "
    ),
    x = "Number of decisions",
    y = NULL,
    caption = ris_graph_caption("Most frequently referenced ECHR norms in Austrian Constitutional Court decisions from 2000 to 2025. Numbers include also references to ECHR Additional Protocols. Short names of the referenced Convention rights are shown in parentheses below each norm.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(
    # must target the leaf element: with ggplot2 4.0 complete themes,
    # axis.text.y gets overridden by the theme's plain axis.text.y.left
    axis.text.y.left = ggtext::element_markdown(
      size = gg_axis_size,
      family = gg_plot_family,
      color = "#263238",
      lineheight = 1.3,
      hjust = 1, # place the label box against the axis
      halign = 1 # right-align lines inside the box
    ),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#D8DEE4", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```


## VwGH - Subsidiary Protection

Let's move on to the next court -- the Verwaltungsgerichtshof (VwGH), Austria's highest court on administrative matters.

An item which has been high on the political and wider public agenda is the question of asylum and migration. As the highest court for administrative matters, the VwGH is the final instance for decisions on asylum and migration. Here, I want to demonstrate how to use the `{risAT}` package to query jurisprudence for a specific legal norm. The `norm` parameter in the function allows the user to search for decisions which cite a specific legal norm. In this example, I will search for decisions which cite `AsylG 2005 §8`, the provision on subsidiary protection.

```{r}
#| label: data-asyl-year
#| code-summary: "Get VwGH data on subsidiary protection "
#| fig-cap: "VwGH search results citing AsylG 2005 §8 by decision year."
#| cache: true

asyl_subsidiary_all <- ris_search_vwgh(
  norm = "'AsylG 2005 §8'",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_legal_principles = F,
  echo = TRUE
)

#check for duplicates
nrow(janitor::get_dupes(asyl_subsidiary_all, id))
glimpse(asyl_subsidiary_all)
```

The resulting graph shows the annual number of decisions by the VwGH which cite `AsylG 2005 §8` (subsidiary protection). The number of decisions citing this norm has been increasing over time, with a notable surge in the early 2020s.

```{r}
#| label: fig-asyl-year
#| code-summary: "Plot data on subsidiary protection by year"
#| fig-cap: "VwGH search results citing AsylG 2005 §8 by decision year."
#| fig-alt: "Column chart showing the yearly number of VwGH search results citing AsylG 2005 section 8 between 2000 and 2025."
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
asyl_by_year <- asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  mutate(year = year(decision_date)) |>
  distinct(year, id) %>%
  count(year, name = "decisions") |>
  complete(year = 2000:2025, fill = list(decisions = 0L)) |>
  arrange(year)

asyl_by_year |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2F6F73", width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(
    data = asyl_by_year |> filter(decisions > 0),
    aes(label = decisions),
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2025, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of decisions by the Austrian Administrative Court (VwGH) referring to 'AsylG 2005 §8' (subsidiary protection)",
    subtitle = "Decisions from 2000 to 2025; Graph reveals a surge of decisions in the wake of the Syrian refugee 'crisis'.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VwGH decisions from 2000 to 2025 citing AsylG 2005 section 8 by decision year.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme()
```

### Query parameter to investigate countries

The graph above shows all decisions pertaining to the norm `AsylG 2005 §8`. We can also combine the search for a specific `norm` with a free text search `query`, which allows to further narrow down the results. In the example below, I add the search term `Afghan* OR Syri* OR Irak*` to capture decisions which relate to Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq.

```{r}
#| label: data-asyl-year-syria
#| code-summary: "Query subsidiary protection decisions related to Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq"
asyl_subsidiary_afghan_syria <- ris_search_vwgh(
  norm = "'AsylG 2005 §8'",
  query="Afghan* OR Syri* OR Irak*",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = T,
  search_legal_principles = F,
  echo = TRUE
)

afghan_syria_ids <- as.character(asyl_subsidiary_afghan_syria$id)

asyl_subsidiary_all <- asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  mutate(
    year = year(decision_date),
    afghan_syria = as.character(id) %in% afghan_syria_ids
  ) 
  
asyl_by_year <- asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  distinct(year, id, afghan_syria) |>
  count(year, afghan_syria, name = "decisions") |>
  complete(
    year = 2000:2025,
    afghan_syria = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    fill = list(decisions = 0L)
  ) |>
  arrange(year, afghan_syria)

asyl_by_year_labels <- asyl_by_year |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    total = sum(decisions),
    afghan_syria_decisions = sum(decisions[afghan_syria]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

asyl_by_year_segment_labels <- asyl_by_year |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(
    total = sum(decisions),
    afghan_syria_pct = if_else(total > 0, decisions / total, NA_real_),
    afghan_syria_label = if_else(
      afghan_syria & decisions > 0,
      scales::percent(afghan_syria_pct, accuracy = 1),
      NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-asyl-year-syria
#| code-summary: "Plot subsidiary protection decisions by year and country group"
#| fig-cap: "VwGH search results citing AsylG 2005 §8 by decision year, highlighting decisions mentioning Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq."
#| fig-alt: "Stacked column chart showing the yearly number of VwGH search results citing AsylG 2005 section 8 between 2000 and 2025, split into decisions mentioning Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq and other decisions, with yearly totals and percentage labels."
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
asyl_by_year |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill=afghan_syria)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  geom_text(
    data = asyl_by_year_labels |> filter(total > 0),
    aes(x = year, y = total, label = total),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = asyl_by_year_segment_labels,
    aes(label = afghan_syria_label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2025, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "#2F6F73", "TRUE" = "#A6544F"),
    labels = c("FALSE" = "Other", "TRUE" = "Afghanistan, Syria, Iraq"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of decisions by the Austrian Administrative Court (VwGH) referring to 'AsylG 2005 §8' (subsidiary protection)",
    subtitle = "Decisions from 2000 to 2025, highlighting decisions mentioning Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VwGH decisions from 2000 to 2025 citing AsylG 2005 section 8 by decision year, highlighting decisions related to Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme()
```

## BVwG - Asylum & Climate Change

Now let's use the query function for a different court, the Bundesverwaltungsgericht (BVwG), the federal administrative court of first instance. Let's again query for the presence of a search term, here 'Klimawandel' (climate change), in the decision text or legal principles. The query covers all years between 2014, the court's first year in operation, up until the end of 2025.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-bvwg-klimawandel
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Get all decisions by the BVwG which contain 'Klimawandel'"
climateChange_bvwg <- ris_search_bvwg(
  query = "Klimawandel",
  decision_date_from = "2014-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: read-bvwg-klimawandel
#| eval: true
#| include: false
#readr::write_rds(climateChange_bvwg, data_path("climateChange_bvwg.rds"), compress = "gz")
climateChange_bvwg <- readr::read_rds(data_path("climateChange_bvwg.rds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-klimawandel-line
#| code-summary: "Plot annual BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel'"
#| fig-cap: "Annual number of BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel'."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart showing the annual number of BVwG decisions mentioning Klimawandel from 2014 to 2025, rising from single digits to a peak in 2024."
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
climateChange_bvwg %>%
  mutate(year=lubridate::year(decision_date)) %>%
  count(year) %>%
  ggplot()+
  labs(title="Annual number of decisions by the BVwG which contain 'Klimawandel'",
  x = NULL,
  y = "Number of decisions",
  caption=ris_graph_caption("Annual number of BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel'."))+
  geom_line(aes(x=year, y=n), color="#7F1D1D")+
  geom_point(aes(x=year, y=n), color="#7F1D1D")+
  geom_text(
    data = \(data) filter(data, year %in% c(2019, 2023, 2024, 2025)),
    aes(x = year, y = n, label = n),
    nudge_x = 0.15,
    hjust = 0,
    color = "black",
    family = gg_plot_family
  )+
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2015, 2020, 2025),
    limits = c(2014, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0), add = c(0, 1))
  )+
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 1))
```

How many of these decisions arise in an asylum context? Analogous to the ECHR example above, we can check the `norms` column for asylum-related norms. The table below shows, per year, the share of 'Klimawandel' decisions which reference such a norm.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-klimawandel-asyl
#| code-summary: "Tabulate BVwG 'Klimawandel' decisions by asylum-norm reference"
#| tbl-cap: "BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel' by year and asylum-norm reference."
climateChange_bvwg <- climateChange_bvwg |>
  mutate(year=year(decision_date)) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_asyl = map_lgl(norms, \(x) any(str_detect(as.character(unlist(x)), regex("Asyl", ignore_case=TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE))
    )

tblclimateChange_bvwg <- climateChange_bvwg %>%
  count(year, norm_asyl) %>%
  mutate(norm_asyl = if_else(norm_asyl, "asylum_norm", "other")) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = norm_asyl, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)  %>%
  complete(year = 2014:2025, fill = list(asylum_norm = 0, other = 0)) %>%
  mutate(
    total = asylum_norm + other,
    asylum_norm_rel = if_else(total > 0, asylum_norm / total, NA_real_)
  )

tblclimateChange_bvwg %>%
  select(year, total, asylum_norm_rel) %>%
  reactable(
    columns = list(
      year = colDef(name = "Year"),
      total = colDef(name = "Total decisions"),
      asylum_norm_rel = colDef(
        name = "Share with asylum norm",
        format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 1)
      )
    ),
    compact = TRUE,
    bordered = TRUE,
    striped = TRUE,
    pagination = FALSE
  )
```

The same split as a chart:

```{r}
#| label: fig-klimawandel-asyl
#| code-summary: "Plot BVwG 'Klimawandel' decisions by asylum-norm reference"
#| fig-cap: "Annual BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel', split by asylum-norm reference."
#| fig-alt: "Stacked column chart of annual BVwG decisions mentioning Klimawandel from 2014 to 2025, split into decisions with and without a reference to an asylum-related norm."
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
tblclimateChange_bvwg %>%
  select(year, asylum_norm, other) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(asylum_norm, other),
    names_to = "decision_group",
    values_to = "decisions"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    decision_group = factor(
      decision_group,
      levels = c("other", "asylum_norm"),
      labels = c("Klimawandel, no asylum norm", "Klimawandel with asylum norm")
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill = decision_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2015, 2020, 2025),
    limits = c(2014, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Klimawandel, no asylum norm" = "#1F3A5F",
      "Klimawandel with asylum norm" = "#D4A017"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "BVwG Klimawandel decisions by asylum-norm reference",
    subtitle = "Annual decisions mentioning Klimawandel, split by whether an asylum-related norm is referenced.",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel' by decision year and asylum-related norm reference.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme()

```

## Equality and discrimination

The Equal Treatment Commission decisions are another useful example because the wrapper exposes domain-specific filters. Instead of only searching text, we can directly filter by discrimination ground. The chart below shows the annual absolute frequency of different discrimination grounds across all years currently available through the RIS GBK endpoint.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-gbk-discrimination
#| code-summary: "Search GBK decisions by discrimination ground and year"
#| cache: true

discrimination_grounds <- c(
  gender = "Gender",
  ethnicity = "Ethnicity",
  religion = "Religion",
  worldview = "Worldview",
  age = "Age",
  sexual_orientation = "Sexual orientation",
  multiple = "Multiple discrimination"
)

gbk_topics <- tibble(
  discrimination_ground = names(discrimination_grounds),
  discrimination_grounds_en = unname(discrimination_grounds)
)


li_gbk_all <- gbk_topics$discrimination_ground |>
  set_names() |>
  map(\(ground) {
    ris_search_gbk(discrimination_ground = ground, echo = TRUE)
  }) 

fn_normalize_lists <- function(df) {
df %>%
  mutate(
    across(any_of(c("id", "application","authority", "document_url","gbk_commission", "gbk_discrimination_ground", "gbk_discrimination_ground_en","gbk_discrimination_offense", "gbk_decision_type", "gk_senate")), as.character),
    across(any_of(c("decision_date", "modified")), as.Date),
    across(any_of(c("norms", "content_urls", "case_number")), as.list)
    )
}

df_gbk_all <- li_gbk_all %>%
  map(., \(x) fn_normalize_lists(x)) %>%
  list_rbind(names_to = "discrimination_ground")

df_gbk_all_year <- df_gbk_all  %>%
  mutate(year = year(decision_date)) %>%
  summarise(decisions = n(), .by = c(year, discrimination_ground)) %>%
  left_join(gbk_topics, by = "discrimination_ground") %>%
  mutate(
    discrimination_grounds_en = factor(
      discrimination_grounds_en,
      levels = unname(discrimination_grounds)
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-gbk-discrimination
#| code-summary: "Plot annual GBK results by discrimination ground"
#| fig-cap: "Annual Equal Treatment Commission search results by discrimination ground."
#| fig-alt: "Faceted bar chart showing annual RIS search result counts for Equal Treatment Commission discrimination grounds: gender, ethnicity, religion, worldview, age, sexual orientation, and multiple discrimination. Each facet heading shows the ground's total count and its share of all results."
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
gbk_plot_data <- df_gbk_all_year %>%
  mutate(ground_total = sum(decisions), .by = discrimination_grounds_en) %>%
  mutate(
    ground_share = ground_total / sum(decisions),
    facet_label = str_glue(
      "{discrimination_grounds_en}: {scales::comma(ground_total)} ({scales::percent(ground_share, accuracy = 0.1)})"
    ),
    facet_label = forcats::fct_reorder(facet_label, as.integer(discrimination_grounds_en))
  )

gbk_fill_palette <- c(
  "Gender" = "#2F6F73",
  "Ethnicity" = "#8A5A44",
  "Religion" = "#6C757D",
  "Worldview" = "#4F5D75",
  "Age" = "#9A6B2F",
  "Sexual orientation" = "#7B6D8D",
  "Multiple discrimination" = "#A6544F"
)

gbk_plot_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill = discrimination_grounds_en)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  facet_wrap(vars(facet_label)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)), labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gbk_fill_palette) +
  labs(
    title = "Discrimination grounds in Equal Treatment Commission decisions",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Annual RIS search results by discrimination ground, ",
      min(gbk_plot_data$year),
      " to ",
      max(gbk_plot_data$year)
    ),
    x = "Decision year",
    y = "RIS search results",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = ris_graph_caption("Equal Treatment Commission search results by discrimination ground and decision year.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_textbox(face = "bold")
  )
```

# Working with the result links

One practical detail is worth highlighting. {risAT} does not only return the fields used in the plots above; it also keeps the links to the original RIS documents. The `content_urls` column is a list-column. Unnesting it gives one row per available format, usually including HTML and PDF.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-content-urls
#| code-summary: "Unnest RIS content URLs"
#| tbl-cap: "Example of unnested RIS content URLs."
asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  prepare_content_urls_table(n = 12) |>
  reactable(
    searchable = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 6,
    bordered = TRUE,
    striped = TRUE,
    compact = TRUE
  )
```

This is helpful for reproducibility. The same pipeline that gets you to a plot can also keep a trace back to the official record.

# What's next

At the moment, {risAT} focuses on the RIS case-law and federal-law endpoints. That already covers a lot: constitutional review, administrative-law disputes, data protection, equality decisions, ordinary court case law, and more. Future work will likely involve broadening API coverage and refining some of the court-specific parameter mappings.

For now, the package is best understood as a pragmatic bridge between RIS and the R workflow: search in a way that remains close to the official system, return data in a shape that is pleasant to work with, and keep links back to the source documents. If you run into bugs or have suggestions, the [issue tracker](https://github.com/werkstattcodes/risAT/issues) is the best place to leave them.

```{r}
knitr::knit_exit()
```

## Prevalence of norms and keywords

```{r}
d <- readRDS(data_path("vfgh", "vfgh_2000_2025.rds")) %>%
  mutate(norms = normalise_norms_column(norms)) %>%
  mutate(asylum = map_lgl(norms, has_matching_norm, pattern = "asyl"))

norms_year <- d %>%
  select(decision_date, norms) %>%
  mutate(year=year(decision_date)) %>%
  unnest_longer(norms) %>%
  group_by(year, norms) %>%
  summarise(decisions=n(), .groups="keep") %>%
  arrange(desc(decisions)) 

keywords_year <- d %>%
  select(decision_date, keywords) %>%
  mutate(year=year(decision_date)) %>%
  mutate(keywords=str_split(keywords, ", ")) %>%
  unnest_longer(keywords) %>%
  filter(!is.na(keywords), keywords != "") %>%
  group_by(year, keywords) %>%
  summarise(decisions=n(), .groups="keep")

keywords_top3 <- keywords_year %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  slice_max(decisions, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(year, keywords) %>%
  mutate(top_keyword = TRUE)

keywords_year_plot <- keywords_year %>%
  left_join(keywords_top3, by = c("year", "keywords")) %>%
  mutate(keyword_group = if_else(coalesce(top_keyword, FALSE), keywords, "Other")) %>%
  group_by(year, keyword_group) %>%
  summarise(decisions = sum(decisions), .groups = "drop")

keyword_levels <- keywords_year_plot %>%
  filter(keyword_group != "Other") %>%
  distinct(keyword_group) %>%
  arrange(keyword_group) %>%
  pull(keyword_group)

keyword_palette <- c(
  setNames(grDevices::hcl.colors(length(keyword_levels), "Dark 3"), keyword_levels),
  Other = "#B8C4C2"
)

keywords_year_plot %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = factor(year),
    y = decisions,
    fill = keyword_group
  )) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = keyword_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(
    title = "Top VfGH keywords by decision year",
    subtitle = "Each column shows the total number of decisions. The three most frequent keywords per year are shown separately; all remaining keywords are grouped as Other.",
    x = "Decision year",
    y = "Decisions",
    fill = "Keyword",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VfGH search results from 2000 to 2025 by keyword and decision year.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.35, "lines")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3, override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white")))
```

```{r}
#| label: fetch-helpers
#| include: false
dir.create(data_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

years <- 2000:2025
year_bounds <- tibble(
  year = years,
  date_from = str_c(year, "-01-01"),
  date_to = str_c(year, "-12-31")
)

fetch_year_by_year <- function(search_fn, prefix, year_bounds, data_dir) {
  pwalk(year_bounds, \(year, date_from, date_to) {
    out_file <- file.path(data_dir, str_c(prefix, "_", year, ".rds"))
    if (file.exists(out_file)) {
      return(invisible(NULL))
    }

    result <- tryCatch(
      search_fn(
        decision_date_from = date_from,
        decision_date_to = date_to,
        search_decision_text = TRUE,
        search_legal_principles = TRUE,
        echo = TRUE
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        warning("Skipping ", prefix, " ", year, ": ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
        NULL
      }
    )

    if (!is.null(result)) {
      saveRDS(result, out_file)
    }
  })
}

combine_year_files <- function(prefix, year_bounds, data_dir) {
  years <- year_bounds$year

  files <- tibble(
    file = list.files(data_dir, str_c("^", prefix, "_[0-9]{4}\\.rds$"), full.names = TRUE)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      file_name = basename(file),
      file_year = as.integer(str_match(file_name, str_c("^", prefix, "_([0-9]{4})\\.rds$"))[, 2])
    ) %>%
    arrange(file_year)

  by_year <- files %>%
    mutate(data = map(file, readRDS))

  combined <- by_year %>%
    transmute(
      file_name,
      file_year,
      data = map2(data, file_year, \(x, year) mutate(x, source_year = year))
    ) %>%
    pull(data) %>%
    list_rbind()

  file_checks <- by_year %>%
    transmute(
      file_name,
      file_year,
      rows = map_int(data, nrow),
      columns = map_int(data, ncol),
      min_decision_date = as.Date(map_chr(data, \(x) as.character(min(x$decision_date, na.rm = TRUE)))),
      max_decision_date = as.Date(map_chr(data, \(x) as.character(max(x$decision_date, na.rm = TRUE)))),
      date_year_mismatches = map2_int(
        data,
        file_year,
        \(x, year) sum(!is.na(x$decision_date) & lubridate::year(x$decision_date) != year)
      )
    )

  missingness <- combined %>%
    summarise(across(
      everything(),
      \(x) {
        if (is.list(x)) {
          sum(map_lgl(x, \(value) is.null(value) || length(value) == 0 || all(is.na(value))))
        } else {
          sum(is.na(x))
        }
      }
    )) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "missing_rows") %>%
    mutate(
      total_rows = nrow(combined),
      missing_share = missing_rows / total_rows
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(missing_rows), column)

  list(
    data = combined,
    completeness_checks = list(
      expected_years = years,
      available_years = files$file_year,
      missing_years = setdiff(years, files$file_year),
      file_checks = file_checks,
      duplicate_ids = combined %>%
        count(id, name = "rows") %>%
        filter(!is.na(id), rows > 1) %>%
        arrange(desc(rows), id),
      missingness = missingness
    )
  )
}
```

## Climate change

Climate litigation is still a comparatively small field in Austria, but searching case law for climate-related language is a useful entry point into rights-based environmental claims, public-law litigation, and administrative disputes.

The following query searches the Constitutional Court for `Klimawandel`. Again, because this is a potentially broad `query` search, I use explicit date bounds and restrict the live example to Rechtssaetze.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-klimawandel
#| code-summary: "Search VfGH decisions for Klimawandel"
#| cache: true
climateChange_vfgh <- ris_search_vfgh(
  query = "Klimawandel",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
) %>%
  mutate(year=year(decision_date))

climateChange_vwgh <- ris_search_vwgh(
  query = "Klimawandel",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
)%>%
  mutate(year=year(decision_date))

climateChange_bvwg <- ris_search_bvwg(
  query = "Klimawandel",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
)%>%
  mutate(year=year(decision_date))

dplyr::bind_rows(
climateChange_vwgh %>% select(year, authority),
climateChange_vfgh %>% select(year, authority),
climateChange_bvwg %>% select(year, authority)
) %>%
  group_by(year, authority) %>%
  summarise(decisions=n(), .groups="keep") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=decisions, fill=authority)) +
  geom_col(position="stack") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(2000,2025,5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Climate change in Austrian case law",
    subtitle = "Search: query = 'Klimawandel', decisions from 2000 to 2025",
    x = "Decision year",
    y = "RIS search results",
    fill = "Court / body",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VfGH and VwGH search results for 'Klimawandel' by decision year.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme()+
  facet_wrap(~authority, scales="free_y") +
  theme(legend.position="none")
```

### Asylum-related norms

```{r}
vwgh_2000_2025 <- readRDS(data_path("vwgh", "vwgh_2000_2025.rds")) %>%
  mutate(norms = normalise_norms_column(norms))

vwgh_norms_long <- vwgh_2000_2025 %>%
  select(id, decision_date, source_year, norms) %>%
  unnest_longer(norms, keep_empty = TRUE)

vwgh_decision_asylum <- vwgh_norms_long %>%
  mutate(has_asylum_norm = str_detect(norms, regex("asyl", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>%
  group_by(id, decision_date, source_year) %>%
  summarise(
    has_asylum_norm = any(has_asylum_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(decision_date),
    asylum_norm = if_else(has_asylum_norm, "Contains Asyl norm", "Other decisions")
  ) %>%
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

vwgh_asylum_by_year <- vwgh_decision_asylum %>%
  count(year, asylum_norm, name = "decisions")

vwgh_asylum_by_year %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = year,
    y = decisions,
    fill = asylum_norm
  )) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2025, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Contains Asyl norm" = "#C94C4C",
      "Other decisions" = "#B8C4C2"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "VwGH decisions with asylum-related norms",
    subtitle = "Each decision is counted once per year. Highlighted decisions contain 'asyl' in at least one norm.",
    x = "Decision year",
    y = "Decisions",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VwGH decisions from 2000 to 2025 by decision year and asylum-related norm reference.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white")))

```

## Comparing courts

The three charts above use the same construction, so it is useful to put them side by side on a shared decision-year axis. BVwG only started operating in 2014, so its panel shows empty columns for 2000-2013 rather than starting later than the other two courts. Each bar is annotated with the total number of decisions for that year, and the asylum-related segment is labelled with its share of that year's total.

```{r}
#| label: fig-courts-comparison
#| code-summary: "Compare asylum-related norms across VwGH, VfGH and BVwG"
#| fig-cap: "Asylum-related norms by court, decision year, and share of yearly decisions."
#| fig-alt: "Three stacked column charts comparing VwGH, VfGH and BVwG decisions by year, split into decisions with and without an asylum-related norm, annotated with yearly totals and the asylum share of each year."
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
count_asylum_by_year <- function(data, min_year = NULL) {
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(norms = normalise_norms_column(norms))

  norms_long <- data %>%
    select(id, decision_date, norms) %>%
    unnest_longer(norms, keep_empty = TRUE)

  decision_asylum <- norms_long %>%
    mutate(has_asylum_norm = str_detect(norms, regex("asyl", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>%
    group_by(id, decision_date) %>%
    summarise(has_asylum_norm = any(has_asylum_norm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(
      year = year(decision_date),
      asylum_norm = if_else(has_asylum_norm, "Contains Asyl norm", "Other decisions")
    ) %>%
    distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

  if (!is.null(min_year)) {
    decision_asylum <- decision_asylum %>% filter(year >= min_year)
  }

  decision_asylum %>%
    count(year, asylum_norm, name = "decisions")
}

courts_by_year_raw <- bind_rows(
  count_asylum_by_year(vwgh_2000_2025) %>% mutate(court = "VwGH"),
  count_asylum_by_year(vfgh_2000_2025) %>% mutate(court = "VfGH"),
  count_asylum_by_year(bvwg_2000_2025) %>% mutate(court = "BVwG")
)

courts_by_year <- expand_grid(
  court = c("VwGH", "VfGH", "BVwG"),
  year = 2000:2025,
  asylum_norm = c("Contains Asyl norm", "Other decisions")
) %>%
  left_join(courts_by_year_raw, by = c("court", "year", "asylum_norm")) %>%
  mutate(
    decisions = coalesce(decisions, 0L),
    court = factor(court, levels = c("VwGH", "VfGH", "BVwG")),
    asylum_norm = factor(asylum_norm, levels = c("Contains Asyl norm", "Other decisions"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(court, year, desc(asylum_norm)) %>%
  group_by(court, year) %>%
  mutate(
    ymax = cumsum(decisions),
    ymin = ymax - decisions,
    ymid = (ymin + ymax) / 2,
    total = sum(decisions),
    pct = if_else(total > 0, decisions / total, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

courts_by_year %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill = asylum_norm)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  geom_text(
    data = courts_by_year %>% distinct(court, year, total) %>% filter(total > 0),
    aes(x = year, y = total, label = scales::comma(total)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 2.9,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = courts_by_year %>% filter(asylum_norm == "Contains Asyl norm", decisions > 0),
    aes(x = year, y = ymid, label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 1)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "white",
    size = 2.6,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~court, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Contains Asyl norm" = "#C94C4C",
      "Other decisions" = "#B8C4C2"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Asylum-related norms across courts",
    subtitle = "Bars are labelled with the total decisions per year; the asylum-related segment shows its share of that year's total.",
    x = "Decision year",
    y = "Decisions",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VwGH, VfGH and BVwG decisions by decision year and asylum-related norm reference. BVwG was only created in 2014, hence the empty columns before that year.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white")))
```

## BVwG: Asylum decisions and climate change

A norm search only tells you what a decision cites, not what it discusses. To see whether climate change comes up inside asylum-related BVwG decisions, the approach is: first take all BVwG decisions with an asylum-related norm (a local filter on data already downloaded), then run a live full-text query against RIS for "Klimawandel" (covering both decision text and legal principles), and left-join the asylum-norm decisions against that query's decision IDs. The result is a boolean flag on the asylum-norm subset, not a new fetch of decisions themselves.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-bvwg-asyl-climate
#| code-summary: "Cross-reference BVwG asylum-norm decisions with a Klimawandel full-text query"
#| eval: false
bvwg_asyl <- bvwg_2000_2025 %>%
  filter(map_lgl(norms, has_matching_norm, pattern = "asyl"))

climate_bvwg <- ris_search_bvwg(
  query = "Klimawandel",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
)

bvwg_asyl_climate <- bvwg_asyl %>%
  left_join(
    climate_bvwg %>% select(id) %>% mutate(mentions_klimawandel = TRUE),
    by = "id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(mentions_klimawandel = coalesce(mentions_klimawandel, FALSE))

saveRDS(bvwg_asyl_climate, file.path(data_dir, "bvwg_asyl_climate.rds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bvwg-asyl-climate
#| code-summary: "Plot BVwG asylum-norm decisions mentioning Klimawandel by year"
#| fig-cap: "BVwG asylum-related decisions by year, highlighting those mentioning 'Klimawandel'."
#| fig-alt: "Stacked column chart of BVwG decisions with an asylum-related norm by decision year, with a highlighted segment for decisions whose text or legal principles mention Klimawandel."
#| column: body-outset-right
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svg_noto
#| fig-ext: svg
bvwg_asyl_climate <- readRDS(data_path("bvwg_asyl_climate.rds")) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(decision_date),
    mention_group = if_else(mentions_klimawandel, "Mentions Klimawandel", "Other asylum-related decisions")
  )

bvwg_asyl_climate_by_year <- bvwg_asyl_climate %>%
  count(year, mention_group, name = "decisions") %>%
  mutate(mention_group = factor(mention_group, levels = c("Mentions Klimawandel", "Other asylum-related decisions")))

year_totals <- bvwg_asyl_climate_by_year %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(decisions), .groups = "drop")

climate_counts <- bvwg_asyl_climate_by_year %>%
  filter(mention_group == "Mentions Klimawandel", decisions > 0) %>%
  left_join(year_totals, by = "year")

bvwg_asyl_climate_by_year %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill = mention_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  geom_text(
    data = climate_counts,
    aes(x = year, y = total, label = scales::comma(decisions)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 2.9,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2014, 2025, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1)), labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Mentions Klimawandel" = "#2F6F73",
      "Other asylum-related decisions" = "#B8C4C2"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Climate change mentions in BVwG asylum decisions",
    subtitle = "All BVwG decisions citing an asylum-related norm, split by whether the decision text or legal principles mention 'Klimawandel'. Labels show the count of decisions mentioning Klimawandel.",
    x = "Decision year",
    y = "Decisions",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = ris_graph_caption("BVwG decisions with an asylum-related norm, 2014 to 2025, split by full-text mentions of 'Klimawandel'.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white")))
```
